Lisa — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Short answer: we can support your need, but it will be a two-part approach depending on how you want the invoices presented.

Options we typically use (and what I recommend for predictable accounting):
1) GCP-side mapping: Partner (Google) creates the private offer and maps SKUs to the specific billing projects you provide — invoices will be issued per-billing-project. This is the cleanest for chargeback but requires Google to enable per-project billing on the offer.
2) Redwood-side reconciliation: If Google issues a single consolidated invoice to the holding company, Redwood can produce a monthly split CSV and a Redwood invoice/credit memo that maps consumption by project and SKU for your finance team. This adds an extra reconciliation step but requires no merchant-side changes.

Immediate ask from our side: please send the three GCP project IDs and the finance contact (name + email) we should copy on the billing handoff. Also confirm whether your tax team requires Redwood's W-9 (we can attach).

Action items I will own:
- Loop in Ben (billing ops) to prepare a SKU-to-project mapping template and an initial proration plan for the first invoice.
- Request Partner Sales to create the private offer with the partner-side mapping as Option 1 if you prefer.
- Share a short playbook (link below) that walks through timeline, DocuSign steps, and expected invoice files.

Links: Playbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=playbook123

I attached an initial SKU mapping template in this thread; Ben will follow up with specifics.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that's easier.

Cheers,

Ben here (Billing Operations). I took a first pass at how we would operationalize both options. TL;DR — Option 1 (Partner-side per-project invoices) is preferred; Option 2 (Redwood reconciliation) is workable and we can automate the monthly CSV.

Technical notes:
- GCP supports billing at the billing-account -> project level. If you provide the three project IDs and confirm ownership, Partner Sales can request per-project invoicing tied to those projects for the private offer.
- For proration on the first invoice we will calculate days-of-service per SKU and include a prorated line in the mapping file.
- If you prefer Redwood reconciliation, we will deliver: 1) a monthly CSV with project_id, sku_id, usage_units, amount_usd, and 2) a Redwood invoice or credit memo to match the PO.

I attached the sku-mapping.csv with example rows for how we expect data. Please replace placeholder project IDs with your real ones and return the file. Once we have that we can:
- Draft the DocuSign amendment to the PO (if needed) to indicate the billing split,
- Set the expected invoice dates (we recommend 1st-of-month for steady bookkeeping),
- Confirm whether your accounting team needs separate tax IDs on each invoice.

Next steps for you (Lisa):
- Send the three GCP project IDs and finance contact (email + billing contact).
- Confirm preferred option (Partner per-project invoices OR Redwood monthly reconciliation).

If helpful, Marissa can run a short run-rate projection showing how the committed units map to monthly charges per project.
